tool_input.content: Verdict: findings. One is CRITICAL and must be fi…
tool_input.message:
Verdict: findings. One is CRITICAL and must be fixed before merge; the rest are lower severity. Full diff reviewed (8 commits, main..HEAD), both mission contracts and the m-2026-10-21-001 reflection/correction trail read, existing 40 (now 46, worker is mid-edit on test file only — hook script itself unchanged since my review) test cases re-run and pass, make lint-shell and shellcheck both clean.

FINDINGS (adversarial, each reproduced directly against .claude/hooks/no-push-to-main.sh):

1. CRITICAL — any git global flag other than `-C` disables the entire gate, not just branch resolution. The command-position regex at line 198 only recognizes `(^|[&|;(])...git...(-C <dir>)*...push`. Any other global option between `git` and `push` — `-c key=val`, `--no-pager`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`, etc. — fails that regex, so the whole hook falls through `|| exit 0` and allows the command with NO check at all, not even the destination-ref check. Reproduced from the plain main checkout itself (no worktree, no redirection trick needed):
   `{"tool_input":{"command":"git -c core.pager=cat push origin main"},"cwd":"<main-checkout-on-main>"}` → empty output (allowed), vs. the same command without `-c` → denied.
   Also confirmed with `git --no-pager push origin main` and with `git --git-dir=<repo>/.git --work-tree=<repo> push origin main`. `-c core.pager=cat` and `--no-pager` are extremely ordinary, not exotic — a developer or an agent habitually suppressing the pager defeats the guard entirely. This is a direct under-deny on the hook's primary purpose.

2. HIGH — multi-`-C` chaining resolves backwards from real git semantics, both directions. Git's own `-C` flags compose cumulatively relative to the previous one (confirmed via `git -C A -C . rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`), but the hook's scope-resolution awk program takes the LAST matched `-C` value verbatim with no composition. For `git -C <dir> -C . push`, real git still resolves to `<dir>` (the `.` is relative to it), and the hook gets this right only by accident when the chain is `<dir> -C .` because `.` composed with `<dir>` is `<dir>` again — but it is fragile: any chain where the final element needs composing with an earlier one (e.g. `-C <worktree>/.. -C repo`) will resolve to the wrong directory. This is a narrower gap than #1 since it only matters when `-C` already matches the regex, but it means the fix for F5 is not fully correct for the general multi-`-C` case the hook's own header comment claims to handle ("this hook does not need to model intermediate hops" — it does, when more than one `-C` is present and any but the last is non-absolute).

3. MEDIUM — command/variable indirection is NOT caught, by design, not a bug, but worth naming since the brief asked about it explicitly: `git $(echo push) origin main`, `g\it push origin main`, `G=git; $G push origin main`, `eval "git push origin main"`, and `xargs git push` are all allowed (hook sees no literal `git ... push` text in command position). These are real gaps but match the hook's documented threat model (lexical classification of the literal command string, not a shell parser) — flagging as MEDIUM because they are easy for a motivated bypass but outside what the regex approach can ever catch without a real shell AST. Worth a comment in the header stating this is out of scope, if it isn't already (it currently is not stated).

4. LOW — `sh -c 'git push origin main'` and `bash -c "git push origin main"` are correctly DENIED (verified) because the inner text still matches in command position within the outer single/double quotes — the stripper's "single word, no internal whitespace → unquote" rule doesn't apply to multi-word quoted interiors containing "push", so these remain caught. No finding here, included only because the brief asked me to check subshell-via-wrapper forms.

5. Tests are honest: all 40/46 cases pass, no over-denies found in my probing (checked `cd subdir && git push`, tab-separated `git push`, newline-separated compound commands, `(subshell)`, background `&`, pipe/semicolon separators — all correctly classified). shellcheck is clean on both scripts. `make check`'s chain (`check: lint lint-strict vulncheck docs test` → `lint: lint-shell vet staticcheck` → `lint-shell: test-shell-discovery test-no-push-to-main-hook`) correctly wires the new test in; confirmed via `make -n check` and an actual `make lint-shell` run.

6. The correction on m-2026-10-21-001 (F5, fixed in the three commits now on branch) is accurate as far as it goes — `-C` and `cd` resolution and fail-closed behavior for non-repo/detached-HEAD are real and tested — but finding #1 above is effectively "F5's sibling," arrived at by the same root cause (the command-position regex enumerates exactly one global flag, `-C`) and was not caught by the F5 fix or its test additions.

RECOMMENDATION: do not close mission m-2026-10-21-005 or merge until #1 is fixed. The cleanest fix given the existing design: change the command-position regex (both the gate at line ~198 and the destination-ref PUSH_ARGS extraction) to allow zero-or-more *arbitrary* git global options before `push` — e.g. a bounded repetition of `(-c <key>=<val>|-C <dir>|--no-pager|--git-dir=<path>|--work-tree=<path>|--literal-pathspecs|...)` is a losing enumeration game; better to match `git` then skip any sequence of tokens that look like options (`-` or `--` prefixed, optionally taking a following bare arg for the space-separated ones) up to the first non-option token, and require that token to be `push`. That also fixes #2 for free if the -C scope walker is reused rather than re-derived. Given the existing awk-based scope resolver already walks -C chains char-by-char, I'd push the worker to generalize "skip over recognized options" into one shared routine used by both the classification gate and the scope resolver, rather than special-casing more flags into three different regexes.

Happy to re-verify once a fix lands — send me the new commit range and I'll re-run the same probes plus a regex-permutation sweep over common git global flags (-c, -C, -p/--paginate, --no-pager, --git-dir, --work-tree, --bare, --no-replace-objects, --literal-pathspecs) to confirm the gate's language covers "any option, not an enumerated list."

tool_input.message:
Evaluator kth finished and the verdict is findings. One is CRITICAL and I reproduced it myself against your current hook, from the main checkout on a feature branch: git -c core.pager=cat push origin main -> ALLOWED git --no-pager push origin main -> ALLOWED git push origin main -> denied (control) git -C /tmp push origin main -> denied Root cause: the command-position regex at ~line 198 enumerates exactly one git global flag, -C. Any other option between git and push (-c key=val, --no-pager, --git-dir=, --work-tree=, -p, --bare, --literal-pathspecs) fails the match, the hook hits `|| exit 0`, and NEITHER check runs. This is F5's sibling: same root cause, missed by the F5 fix and its tests. This is the second gap from the same cause in two rounds, so do not patch the regex with more flags. Required design for this fix: one shared "skip git global options" routine that consumes any sequence of option tokens after `git` (anything starting with - or --, plus the following bare argument for the space-separated forms: -C , -c , --git-dir

, --work-tree

, --namespace , --exec-path

) up to the first non-option token, and requires that token to be `push`. Use that same routine in the classification gate, in the PUSH_ARGS extraction for the destination-ref check, and in the scope resolver, so there is one definition of "where does the subcommand start" instead of three regexes. Second finding, HIGH, fix in the same pass: multiple -C flags must compose left to right like git does (each relative to the previous), not take the last one verbatim. `git -C /.. -C repo push` must resolve to /../repo. Tests: add each of these as deny from a main cwd, under jq and no-jq: -c core.pager=cat, --no-pager, --git-dir=/.git --work-tree=, -p, --literal-pathspecs, and two options stacked (-c x=y --no-pager). Add the composed multi -C case. Add one allow: `git -c core.pager=cat push origin feat/example` from the feature worktree. Keep every existing case green. Also add a short header note that variable and command-substitution indirection ($G push, $(echo push), eval, xargs) is out of scope for a lexical hook; the evaluator flagged its absence. Same discipline: tests first, one commit per step, each passing make check, no push, no PRs. Then submit the result on m-2026-10-21-005 with --verify --base 7b73424 and report the commit list plus the probe results for the four lines above. The evaluator will re-run its flag sweep on your new range.

tool_input.message:
Silent-failure hunt on fix/push-guard-worktree (hook at <repo>/.claude/hooks/no-push-to-main.sh, test at .../no-push-to-main_test.sh). Every finding below was reproduced by feeding crafted PreToolUse JSON to the real hook against a throwaway repo (main checkout on `main`, worktree on `feat`). "ALLOW" means the hook exited 0 with no deny payload. The committed suite (46 cases after 6d723ff) passes 0 failures, and none of these cases are in it. No files edited.

CRITICAL: real fail-open on a missing tool

1. no-push-to-main.sh:198. `grep -qE ... || exit 0`. If grep is absent from PATH, bash prints `grep: command not found`, status 127, and `|| exit 0` turns that into ALLOW. Input: PATH without grep, command `git push origin main`, cwd = feature worktree. Result: ALLOW. The header comment says enforcement "does not depend on jq", but it depends on grep with no fallback at all. Same pattern at lines 334 and 335, though 198 fails first. Fix: check `command -v grep sed awk git` up front and call deny() with a "hook dependency missing" reason, the way the stripper fallback at 185 already treats awk.

2. no-push-to-main.sh:279. `SCOPE=$(... | awk "$RESOLVE_SCOPE_PROGRAM" 2>/dev/null)`. The 2>/dev/null swallows "awk: command not found" (and any awk runtime error). SCOPE is empty, BRANCH_DIR silently falls back to the payload cwd, and the branch check reads the wrong directory. Inputs with awk absent from PATH, cwd = feature worktree: `git -C <main-checkout> push` is ALLOW; `cd <main-checkout> && git push` is ALLOW. This is the inverse of the fail-safe the stripper got at 173-187, and it is exactly the F5 fix this branch claims to close. Fix: capture awk's status like STRIP_STATUS does and deny on non-zero.

HIGH: classification narrows and allows a real push

3. no-push-to-main.sh:150 heredoc detector matches `<<` anywhere on a line, including inside quotes, comments, and here-strings, then drops every following line until the fake delimiter. Each of these two-line commands, cwd = feature worktree, is ALLOW: `cat <<< "x"` newline `git push origin main`; `echo "a <<EOF b"` newline `git push origin main`; `# see <<EOF notes` newline `git push origin main`. The 185 fallback does not fire because CLASSIFY_TEXT is non-empty (first line survives). The comment at 177-181 claims the stripper "can only ever over-match"; this is under-matching.

4. no-push-to-main.sh:198 and :231 recognize only `-C` as a git global flag, and only `&|;(` as a preceding separator. All ALLOW from the feature worktree: `git -c user.name=x push origin main`; `git --no-pager push origin main`; `git --git-dir=<main>/.git --work-tree=<main> push`; `timeout 60 git push origin main`; `command git push origin main`; `if true; then git push origin main; fi`; `{ git push origin main; }`. Also `bash -c 'git push origin main'` and `eval "git push origin main"` are ALLOW because the stripper blanks the multi-word quoted interior (intended for data, but here the data is executed).

5. no-push-to-main.sh:231-275 scope resolution is per line and takes only the FIRST push invocation. All ALLOW, cwd = feature worktree: `cd <main>` newline `git push` (the cd is on the previous line, so prefix is empty); `git push origin feat; git -C <main> push` and `git push origin feat; cd <main>; git push` (match() returns the first invocation, which has no -C/cd); `pushd <main> && git push`; `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=<main> git push`; `cd && git push`. Note PUSH_ARGS at 334 uses grep -o and sees every invocation, so the ref gate handles multiples but the branch gate does not.

6. no-push-to-main.sh:335 destination regex requires `[[:space:]:/]` before main. ALLOW from the feature worktree: `git push origin +main` (force-push refspec, the most dangerous form); `git push origin ma\in`; `git pu\sh origin main`; `git push origin $'main'`; `B=main; git push origin $B`. The first one is a one-character fix (`[[:space:]:/+]`); the backslash and variable cases need either unescaping outside quotes or a deny on unresolvable refs.

MEDIUM: stdout pollution can turn a deny into nothing

7. no-push-to-main.sh:297 and :301 use bare `cd`. With CDPATH set in the environment, bash prints the resolved directory to stdout, and stdout is the hook's JSON decision channel. Reproduced: CDPATH=<parent>, command `cd repo && git push`, cwd on main: stdout is a bare path line followed by the deny JSON. Command `cd subdir && git push origin feat`: stdout is a bare path with no JSON. `git -C - push` prints OLDPWD via `cd -`. If Claude Code fails to parse the mixed stdout, the deny is lost. Fix: `cd -- "$dir" >/dev/null` and clear CDPATH, or use `builtin cd`. Also pass `--` so a directory beginning with `-` is not read as an option.

LOW

8. no-push-to-main.sh:29 and :50-51. If stdin is not JSON, jq prints a parse error to stderr, COMMAND is empty, and the hook ALLOWs. Reproduced with raw `not json at all` on stdin: exit 0, no deny. Claude Code always sends JSON, so practical risk is low, but it is still "parse failure equals allow". If cat is missing, INPUT is empty and the same thing happens.

9. no-push-to-main.sh:53-54. The sed fallback uses greedy `.*"command"` and `.*"cwd"`, so it keys off the LAST occurrence of each key in the payload, and the cwd pattern stops at the first `"` with no escape handling. Works for today's payload shape only.

Test-script issues (vacuous or blind assertions)

10. no-push-to-main_test.sh:344-346 "awk entirely absent" uses `git push origin main`, which the destination-ref gate denies without ever touching awk. It proves nothing about the scope path at hook line 279, which fails open without awk (finding 2). Add `git -C $REPO push` and `cd $REPO && git push` under NOAWK_BIN expecting deny.

11. no-push-to-main_test.sh:114-117 and :302-305. `got` defaults to "allow" and flips to "deny" only on a substring match. A hook that crashes (syntax error, exit 127, missing tool) registers as "allow", so every allow-expected case passes vacuously against a broken hook, and stdout pollution (finding 7) is invisible because only the substring is checked. Assert exit status 0, and assert stdout is exactly empty for allow and exactly one JSON line for deny.

12. no-push-to-main_test.sh:298-299. assert_fallback_decision redirects the hook's stderr to /dev/null, so the "awk entirely absent" probe hides the very `awk: command not found` message that distinguishes "fallback engaged" from "hook silently did nothing". Keep stderr visible or assert on it.

13. no-push-to-main_test.sh:348-350 "TMPDIR unwritable" passes trivially: the hook no longer touches TMPDIR (process substitution uses /dev/fd) and bash 5.1+ backs heredocs under the pipe-buffer size with pipes, not TMPDIR. It is a regression guard against reintroducing mktemp, nothing more. Fine to keep, but it should not be described as exercising a stripper failure mode.

What is genuinely fail-closed and correct: missing git or old git (310-314 deny), unenterable or non-repo or detached directories (297-314 deny), awk missing for the stripper (185 fallback, verified), jq missing (sed path, verified on the committed suite), and multi-line SCOPE output (case glob yields a bogus dir, cd fails, deny).

Recommended minimum before merge: findings 1, 2, 6 (+main), 7, and test fixes 10 and 11. Findings 3-5 are structural (a regex-based shell classifier cannot be made complete) and are worth a documented known-limits section plus the cheap wins listed.
